answer: Adaptive registration throttling with clustering detection resists sybil attacks. When an agent joins, the protocol fingerprints onboarding signals and scores them against existing identities. Inside a detected cluster, its deposit scales with density and a delay is imposed. Like saffron threads picked one by one, each identity bears an unshareable cost. An attacker farming puppets on copper servers sees costs climb as clones reinforce the pattern. A lone agent from a distant dune faces only baseline friction. The attacker must disperse clones or pay premiums exceeding any sybil reward.
